messages:
maya: Heads-up — getting a cluster of p99 complaints from an enterprise customer (Litera) starting ~10:33Z. Symptoms: intermittent ~5–12s tails on text.generate with Dedicated pool dp-litera-us-west. Seen on multiple tenants in the pool. Any immediate fixes?

autoscale-bot: AUTOSCALE_EVENT 2026-03-16T10:33:12Z scale_request id=sr_0ab9 target_gpus=6 pool=dp-litera-us-west status=queued reason=capacity_quota; provision_attempts=3 backoff=2s

maya: Attach latencies spiking during scale-up window. p95 ~900ms but p99 up to 12s according to traces. Root spans show long time in attach_handshake and model_cache_init.

ashwin: Investigating now — looking at provisioner and warmup logs. Initial impression: node allocation returned, but instance attach / ssh handshake is delayed by the infra node agent (we had a recent agent rollout last night).

ashwin: Quick log snippet:
```
provisioner: request=sr_0ab9 allocated_nodes=6
node-agent(us-west-2b): heartbeat=ok
attach-manager: start_attach node=host-az3-09 id=attach_7a time_ms=0
attach-manager: download_model dp-litera-v2 shard=0 status=queued
download-service: connection_reset during streaming chunk=3
attach-manager: attach_complete time_ms=11980 status=ok
```

jessie: Customer reported 500s and timeouts to support at 10:35Z. They've escalated to their SRE. For a short-term workaround I told them we can route new requests to hosted fallback while we stabilize the pool — they'll accept as temporary.

maya: Can we flip incoming routing for Litera to hosted for new sessions? Also we should reduce the attach timeout so client requests fail faster and hit fallback sooner.

sadhna: Two quick mitigations I can push: 1) increase pool min_reserved from 2->4 (forces warmer capacity) 2) enable prewarm for model dp-litera-v2 (kick off model cache download earlier). Both are quick but will consume extra capacity.

nik: Small policy change: reduce attach timeout on gateway from 15s -> 8s and make fallback route priority higher for enterprise customers flagged with emergency_fallback=true.

ashwin: I'll patch autoscaler backoff and jitter — current exponential backoff seems to align nodes provisioned in batches and exacerbates the thundering attach. Adding randomized jitter and shortening initial backoff should smooth ramp.

maya: Jessie, can you coordinate with Litera and confirm the hosted fallback? Also need to capture repro steps and a short packet capture/trace for infra.

jessie: Confirmed — Litera ok with hosted fallback for now. I told them we'll revert when dp-litera is stable. They asked for ETA — said within 2 hours if we can get a clear plan.

ashwin: Actions I'm taking now:
- Rolling back last node-agent change on a small subset in us-west-2 to test impact (will report in 10m).
- Adjusting autoscaler initial_backoff=1s jitter=+/-500ms for pool dp-litera-us-west.
- Increasing logs on download-service to capture chunk failures.

sadhna: Deploying prewarm and bumping min_reserved. Prewarm will trigger model fetch tasks: might take ~3–8m to populate KV caches.

maya: Repro steps I used that hit the tail: (from inside Litera's repro harness)
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Model: dp-litera-v2" \
  -d '{"prompt":"<100 tokens>", "max_tokens":64}' -w '\nTIME:%{time_total}s\n' -o /dev/null
```
Multiple runs hit ~10s on the call, the server trace shows attach->model_download step dominating.

autoscale-bot: NOTE pool dp-litera-us-west current_min_reserved=2 current_capacity_free=0 queued_reqs=37

ashwin: After rolling the agent on a sample subset, attach latency dropped on that subset (p99 -> ~850ms). Suspect the agent rollout introduced a regression in parallel download handling. Root cause likely a resource starvation during parallel model shard downloads.

nik: Okay — immediate mitigations agreed: 1) host-routing for new requests (jessie) 2) prewarm + min_reserved bump (sadhna) 3) agent rollback on affected AZ (ashwin) 4) gateway attach timeout reduction (maya/infra) 5) autoscaler jitter tweak (ashwin). Assign owners and ETA 2h.

maya: I've applied the gateway timeout patch (15s->8s) and increased fallback priority. We'll monitor error budget and request counts.

sadhna: Prewarm finished for dp-litera-v2 across the pool. Cache hit rate improving; model_cache_init now <120ms on warmed nodes.

autoscale-bot: pool dp-litera-us-west events: scale_request sr_0ab9 -> nodes_allocated=6 nodes_attached=6 attach_p99=950ms after agent-rollback & prewarm

jessie: Customer reports slower responses initially but mostly routed to hosted and no more 12s tails. They appreciate the quick fallback.

maya: Postmortem checklist:
- short-term: keep min_reserved=4 for 24h, maintain fallback routing for Litera until tomorrow morning.
- medium: run canary of node-agent with concurrency limits for shard downloads.
- long-term: add capacity gating when agent rollout in pool in progress and auto-prewarm for models with active customer flags.

ashwin: I'll open an issue with the agent team and include logs + repro harness. Also will add a metric on parallel_download_failures per node.

nik: I'll draft a short customer-facing note for Litera and share with CSM.

maya: Closing the incident in this thread — will file a follow-up RFC for rollout safety and autoscaler tuning. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
